clue.text: Ridicule a form of transport, then, switching sides, rely on it

parts.note: rail is a form of transport, travel by train

indicators.note: the letters on the right and left of the word rely trade places, a swap of sides

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a means of travel, then changes their mind and depends on it.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords R and L stand for right and left, the two sides, so 'switching sides' trades those two letters; 'then' and 'on it' only place the second piece after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Raillery is good-humoured teasing or banter, a mild kind of mockery.

clue.text: Are the poorly to become feverish again?

indicators.note: poorly means unwell or badly made, so the letters of these two words are put together badly

explanation.surface: A question whether the sick are about to run a temperature once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To reheat is to make or grow hot a second time, as a relapsing patient's temperature rises.

clue.text: Signal to bring in social worker

parts.note: to import is to bring goods in from abroad
an ant is a social insect and a worker in its colony

explanation.surface: A sign summoning a welfare officer to come in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Signal' is the definition as an adjective (a signal victory), not a sign; the ant is a social worker in the insect sense.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective signal means notable or outstanding, a near synonym of momentous.

clue.text: Old tear ruined tight garment

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters of old tear are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: An aged rip has spoilt a close-fitting piece of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A leotard is a close-fitting one-piece costume worn by dancers and gymnasts.

clue.text: Country sport gunmen finally left

parts.note: RU is short for rugby union, a sport
RA is the Royal Artillery, soldiers who man the guns

explanation.surface: Rural pursuits: gunmen leave at the end of the day's sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' is the adjective here (country life), not a nation; 'finally' only says L comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural means relating to the countryside rather than the town.

clue.text: Fish doctor caught in Arctic region

indicators.note: one thing caught in another sits inside it, so the doctor goes within the fish

parts.note: the tuna is a large sea fish

explanation.surface: A medic snared inside a fish in the far north.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is the vast treeless plain of the Arctic, with frozen subsoil.

clue.text: Vulgar female has abandoned unclad youth

indicators.note: abandoned means left behind, so these letters are dropped from the run of the last two words

parts.note: a lady is a female person

explanation.surface: A coarse woman has walked out on a naked young man.
explanation.walkthrough: Write out UNCLADYOUTH and take out LADY from the middle to leave UNCOUTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncouth means lacking manners or refinement, which is what vulgar describes.

clue.text: Many in RADA involved in this

definitions.text: Many in RADA involved in this

indicators.note: the thousand sits inside the name of the London acting academy
involved means tangled up, so the letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: M, the Roman numeral for a thousand, stands for many

explanation.surface: Lots of students at the drama school take part in this art form.
explanation.walkthrough: RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in London; put M inside it to get RAMDA and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Students at RADA are engaged in theatre, the acting of plays.

clue.text: If not on track, they could be for the high jump

definitions.text: If not on track, they could be for the high jump

parts.words: If not on track, they could be for the high jump
parts.note: 'for the high jump' reads like 'about to be punished', but these are sports competitors who, when not running on the track, take part in field events like the high jump

explanation.surface: People who have gone off course may be in serious trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Sportspeople in track and field events either run on the track or jump and throw.

clue.text: His work is caring, and his charges low

definitions.text: His work is caring, and his charges low

parts.words: His work is caring, and his charges low
parts.note: reads like a cheap carer, but the charges are cattle that low, the sound a cow makes

explanation.surface: A nurse whose job is looking after people and who asks a small fee.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockman is a farm hand who looks after livestock such as cows.

clue.text: Medical undertaking to chap I repeatedly treated? That's about right

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, around, the letter for right
treated means processed or worked on, so the letters are reworked
repeatedly says the three words are taken twice over

explanation.surface: A doctor's vow given to a man, offered twice, seems about right.
explanation.walkthrough: Take TOCHAPI twice, rearrange the fourteen letters, and put R in among them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hippocratic oath is the solemn promise of ethical conduct traditionally made by new doctors.

clue.text: Correspondence carried out at high level

definitions.text: Correspondence carried out at high level

parts.words: Correspondence carried out at high level
parts.note: sounds like talks between senior officials, but it is letters literally carried high up, through the sky

explanation.surface: Letters exchanged between top-ranking officials.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmail is post carried by aircraft.

clue.text: Brecht's mother is about as old as we are

parts.note: C, from Latin circa, means about
something as old as we are is of our age

explanation.surface: A question of the age of a playwright's mother compared with ours.
explanation.walkthrough: Mother Courage and Her Children is a play by Bertolt Brecht; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Brecht's play is known as Mother Courage.

clue.text: Spice queen, maybe an old lady in America

parts.note: a queen is an example of a playing card
in American English mom is mother, one's old lady

explanation.surface: A royal, or perhaps an elderly US woman, flavours the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardamom is an aromatic seed used as a spice in curries and baking.

clue.text: Expose scandal that spreads across the land

definitions.meaning: to search out and publish wrongdoing by public figures
a farm tool for spreading manure over fields

explanation.surface: A journalist's exposure of corruption spreads across the country.
explanation.definitionFit: To muckrake is to dig up scandal, and a muck rake is a farm rake for dung.

clue.text: Paradoxically, it's more liable to cut rates

definitions.text: Paradoxically, it's more liable to cut rates

parts.words: Paradoxically, it's more liable to cut rates
parts.note: a shop's discounting suggests itself, but the proverb 'more ... less speed' says hurrying slows you down, cutting your rate

explanation.surface: Strangely, a firm is more likely to slash its prices.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurrying, or rush, is what the proverb says reduces speed.

clue.text: Vocalist needs rare arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things in a new order, as with these letters

explanation.surface: A singer requires an unusual musical arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenader is one who sings, especially beneath a lover's window.

clue.text: Architectural feature, substantial part of farmhouse, say

definitions.meaning: the raised step at the entrance of a building
a farmhouse is a type of loaf, and a thick slice from one is called by this name

explanation.surface: A building detail that makes up much of a farmhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a farmhouse loaf is a type of bread, and a very thick slice of bread is called a doorstep.
explanation.definitionFit: A step at a front door is part of a building, and a very thick slice of bread has the same name.

clue.text: Senior citizen holding books available

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the books sit inside the pensioner

parts.note: OAP is old-age pensioner
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: An elderly person has library books ready to lend.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on tap is ready for use whenever wanted, like beer from a barrel.

clue.text: Some of these cans are open

definitions.text: Some of these cans are open

parts.words: Some of these cans are open
parts.note: reads like tins with lids off, but can is slang for jail, and some jails are open, with minimal security

explanation.surface: A few of the tins have had their lids removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Can is slang for a jail, and open jails let inmates out to work.

clue.text: Enforcer changes associate

indicators.note: changes means alters, so the letters of the first word are altered in order

explanation.surface: A heavy alters his partner in crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A confrere is a fellow member of a profession or society, a colleague.

clue.text: Unwinds thread half-heartedly and then cuts

indicators.note: the heart of the word is halved, losing one of its two central letters

parts.note: to reel is to wind thread on a spool, and a reel holds thread
axes are cuts, as in budget cuts

explanation.surface: Someone loosens yarn without enthusiasm, then snips it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' drops one of the two E's in the middle of REEL, leaving REL.
explanation.definitionFit: To relax is to unwind, to rest and let tension go.

clue.text: The rich and the upwardly mobile

definitions.meaning: wealthy, fashionable people who travel the world
literally, things that rise into the air

explanation.surface: Wealthy people and those climbing the social ladder.
explanation.definitionFit: The jet set are glamorous rich travellers, and jets climb high.

clue.text: More turned on king, and I on queen

parts.note: R, for Latin rex, means king
ER, Elizabeth Regina, means queen

explanation.surface: An aroused royal: the king, with me riding on the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' means 'next after' twice over in a down-style charade; ER is a conventional crossword queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Randier means more lustful, more sexually aroused.

clue.text: Relative novice irritates expert chef, eating starters

indicators.note: starters are the first letters of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: A new cook annoys the head chef, who keeps eating appetisers.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a sibling's daughter, a family member.

clue.text: Proverbially golden, but it appears 50% silver from 'ere

indicators.note: fifty per cent of the word is its first half, three letters of six

parts.note: from here is hence, and 'ere drops its H, so it is said 'ence

explanation.surface: Quiet is proverbially gold, but here it looks half silver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speech is silver, silence is golden' is the proverb; the dropped H in 'ere signals HENCE losing its H.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says speech is silver but quiet, saying nothing, is golden.

clue.text: Capital seat that appears to engulf one

indicators.note: to engulf is to swallow up, so the seat wraps round the one

parts.note: a sofa is an upholstered seat
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A capital city with a seat that seems to swallow someone up.
explanation.definitionFit: Sofia is the capital city of Bulgaria.

clue.text: Early flight recorder

parts.note: sounds like an aircraft black box, but the flight is the Israelites' escape from Egypt, recorded in the Bible

explanation.surface: An early aviation data recorder, a pioneer's black box.
explanation.definitionFit: The second book of the Old Testament tells of the Israelites fleeing Egypt.

clue.text: Place with comfort to give satisfaction

parts.note: PL is a common abbreviation for place in street names
ease is comfort, freedom from worry

explanation.surface: A comfortable spot will gratify you.
explanation.definitionFit: To please is to delight or gratify someone.

clue.text: Classical language lacking academic analysis, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: sans is French for without, lacking, and a crit is an academic critique

explanation.surface: An ancient tongue untouched by scholarly criticism, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanskrit is the ancient literary language of India.
